name: Jotham
overview: Jotham was a male member of the tribe of Manasseh, known as the youngest son of Gideon (Jerubbaal). He is notably recognized as the sole survivor of the violent fratricide committed by Abimelech against his brothers. This unique circumstance highlights Jotham's distinct place within his family and Israel's history.
namesAndTitles: The name Jotham means 'YHWH will complete,' reflecting a trust in God's faithful fulfillment of His purposes. This proper name, recorded in Judges 9:5, was not given by God directly but carries a meaningful Hebrew significance.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Jotham was the son of Gideon, also known as Jerubbaal. Beyond this father-son relationship, no other family connections are documented in the provided facts.
scriptureSignificance: Jotham's survival amid his brothers' massacre by Abimelech marks him as a significant figure in the narrative of Israel's judges. His experience underscores the consequences of human ambition and violence within God's chosen people. Jotham's story also serves as a reminder that God's plans persist even through trials and familial strife, pointing to His sovereign completion of His purposes.
